title_es: Conectores (linking words): unir ideas para explicar un proceso, dar razones y contrastar
explanation_es:
Los conectores (linking words) unen ideas para que no hables con frases sueltas. En el examen oral son la clave del criterio de secuencia lineal cohesionada: el instructor quiere oír first, then, after that y finally.

Hay cinco familias. Contraste: but, however, on the other hand. Comparación y ejemplos: like, similarly, in the same way para comparar, y such as para dar ejemplos. Tiempo y secuencia: first o firstly, secondly, then, next, after that, before, later, finally. Adición: and, also, as well as, not only... but also, moreover. Causa y efecto: because, because of y due to dan la causa; so, therefore, as a result y consequently dan el resultado.

Cómo se usan: el conector no cambia en afirmativa, negativa o pregunta; cambian la posición y la puntuación. And, but, so y because unen dos ideas en la misma oración: I use MySQL because it is free. However, therefore, moreover y as a result suelen abrir una oración nueva, con punto antes, mayúscula y coma después: I like Python. However, my project uses Java. Due to y because of van seguidos de un sustantivo, nunca de sujeto más verbo: due to the rain.

Lo que más confunde: en español es común poner sin embargo entre comas en medio de la frase, pero en inglés however no une dos oraciones con una simple coma como but. So equivale a así que o a entonces cuando indica consecuencia; el entonces de tiempo (luego) es then. Y after no va solo al empezar un paso como después: se dice after that o afterwards.

Señales para la parte escrita: antes de un sustantivo, due to o because of; antes de sujeto y verbo que dan una razón, because; después de punto y seguido de coma, However, Therefore, Moreover o As a result; ideas opuestas, but u on the other hand; un resultado, so; un paso de un proceso, first, then, next o finally.

contrast.en: I wanted to use PHP, but my team chose Java.
contrast.es: Quería usar PHP, pero mi equipo eligió Java.
contrast.note_es: But une las dos ideas en una sola oración, con coma antes. No lleva punto ni mayúscula. Es el contraste más simple y seguro para hablar.

contrast.en: Working from home is comfortable. However, it is easy to get distracted.
contrast.es: Trabajar desde casa es cómodo. Sin embargo, es fácil distraerse.
contrast.note_es: However abre una oración nueva: punto antes, mayúscula y coma después. No lo pongas entre dos ideas solo con coma como si fuera but.

contrast.en: The system was slow because the database had no indexes.
contrast.es: El sistema estaba lento porque la base de datos no tenía índices.
contrast.note_es: Because va seguido de sujeto y verbo (the database had). Da la razón, no el resultado. Es el que más vas a usar para responder preguntas con Why.

contrast.en: The meeting was cancelled due to a power cut.
contrast.es: La reunión se canceló debido a un corte de luz.
contrast.note_es: Due to va seguido de un sustantivo (a power cut), nunca de sujeto y verbo. Si lo que sigue tiene verbo, cambia a because: because the power went out.

contrast.en: The server crashed, so we lost the data. As a result, we now make backups every day.
contrast.es: El servidor se cayó, así que perdimos los datos. Por eso, ahora hacemos copias de seguridad todos los días.
contrast.note_es: So y as a result indican resultado (así que, por eso, en consecuencia). So une dos ideas en una sola oración, con coma antes; as a result empieza una oración nueva y lleva coma después.

contrast.en: First, I download the installer. Then I run it. After that, I accept the terms. Finally, I click Install.
contrast.es: Primero, descargo el instalador. Luego lo ejecuto. Después de eso, acepto los términos. Por último, hago clic en Instalar.
contrast.note_es: Esta es la cadena para describir un proceso paso a paso en el oral. First, after that y finally llevan coma; then puede ir con o sin coma. Fíjate que después solo al inicio se dice after that, no after.

contrast.en: I use tools such as Git and MySQL, as well as Visual Studio Code.
contrast.es: Uso herramientas como Git y MySQL, además de Visual Studio Code.
contrast.note_es: Such as presenta ejemplos, igual que como o por ejemplo en español (es un poco más formal que like). As well as suma un elemento más, parecido a and pero un poco más formal.

common_errors.wrong: I like this job, however the salary is low.
common_errors.right: I like this job. However, the salary is low.
common_errors.why_es: En español es común escribir sin embargo en medio de la frase solo entre comas. En inglés, however no une dos oraciones con una coma como but: necesita punto antes y coma después. Si quieres una sola oración con coma, usa but: I like this job, but the salary is low.

common_errors.wrong: The class was cancelled due to the instructor was sick.
common_errors.right: The class was cancelled because the instructor was sick.
common_errors.why_es: Due to solo acepta un sustantivo después (due to the rain). Si lo que sigue tiene sujeto y verbo (the instructor was sick), el conector correcto es because.

common_errors.wrong: I chose ADSO because of I like programming.
common_errors.right: I chose ADSO because I like programming.
common_errors.why_es: Because of va con sustantivo (because of the schedule); because va con sujeto y verbo. Recuerda: because of es a causa de o por; because es porque.

common_errors.wrong: I open the program. After, I click Save.
common_errors.right: I open the program. After that, I click Save.
common_errors.why_es: En español decimos después solo, pero en inglés after no puede quedar suelto al inicio de la oración. Necesita complemento (after that, after the installation) o cámbialo por then o afterwards.

common_errors.wrong: I not only test the code but too I document it.
common_errors.right: I not only test the code but also document it.
common_errors.why_es: La pareja fija es not only... but also, que equivale a no solo... sino también. Too va al final de una frase (I document it too), no dentro de esta estructura.

common_errors.wrong: Because the internet was slow, so we couldn't upload the project.
common_errors.right: Because the internet was slow, we couldn't upload the project.
common_errors.why_es: En español decimos como el internet estaba lento, entonces no pudimos. En inglés no se usan because y so en la misma oración: because da la causa y so el resultado, así que eliges uno. También vale: The internet was slow, so we couldn't upload the project.

common_errors.wrong: In the other hand, working from home saves money.
common_errors.right: On the other hand, working from home saves money.
common_errors.why_es: Es una traducción directa de por otro lado, pero la expresión fija en inglés es on the other hand, con on. Con in es un error y el instructor lo nota de inmediato.

oral_questions.question: Can you explain how you install a program step by step?
oral_questions.model_answer: First, I download the installer from the official website. Then I run it and accept the terms. After that, I choose the folder, and finally I click Install.
oral_questions.focus: Secuencia para describir un proceso: first, then, after that, finally.

oral_questions.question: Why did you choose software development?
oral_questions.model_answer: I chose it because I like solving problems with code. Also, there are many jobs in this area, so I think it is a good option for the future.
oral_questions.focus: Causa y efecto: because, so; adición: also.

oral_questions.question: What are two advantages and one disadvantage of working from home?
oral_questions.model_answer: Working from home saves time and money because I don't have to travel. On the other hand, it is easy to get distracted at home.
oral_questions.focus: Adición y contraste: and, because, on the other hand.

oral_questions.question: How does your access-control project register a visitor?
oral_questions.model_answer: First, the guard asks for the visitor's ID and types it into the system. Next, the system checks the database and prints a badge. After that, the visitor can enter the center.
oral_questions.focus: Proceso paso a paso de tu proyecto: first, next, after that.

oral_questions.question: What tools do you use in your project, and why?
oral_questions.model_answer: I use tools such as MySQL for the database and Java for the backend. I chose MySQL because it is free and my instructor recommended it.
oral_questions.focus: Ejemplos con such as; razón con because.

oral_questions.question: Which do you prefer, frontend or backend? Why?
oral_questions.model_answer: I prefer backend because I like working with databases. However, frontend is also important, so I am learning both.
oral_questions.focus: Contraste con however; resultado con so.

oral_questions.question: When do you study English, and how do you organize your time?
oral_questions.model_answer: I study English at night, after my SENA classes. First, I review vocabulary. Then I do some exercises, and finally I practice speaking for ten minutes.
oral_questions.focus: Secuencia: first, then, finally; tiempo: after más sustantivo (after my classes).

oral_questions.question: What happened the last time your code didn't work?
oral_questions.model_answer: Last week my program didn't compile due to a missing semicolon, so I lost an hour. Therefore, I now check my code carefully before I run it.
oral_questions.focus: Causa y efecto en pasado: due to más sustantivo, so, therefore.

oral_questions.question: Who helps you with your project, and how do you divide the work?
oral_questions.model_answer: My team helps me. One classmate designs the database, and I write the code. Moreover, we not only test the app but also document it.
oral_questions.focus: Adición: and, moreover, not only... but also.

oral_questions.question: Where would you like to work after SENA, and what is one difficulty?
oral_questions.model_answer: I would like to work in a software company in Bogotá. However, there is a lot of competition, so I need to keep learning.

roleplay.situation_es: Estás presentando el sistema de control de acceso al coordinador del centro de formación, que hace el papel de cliente. Él quiere entender el proceso paso a paso y por qué tomaste algunas decisiones. Usa conectores de secuencia, causa, adición y contraste; el instructor evalúa que conectes los pasos en orden.

lines.speaker: Client
lines.line: Good morning. Can you explain how the system registers a new visitor?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: Of course. First, the guard asks for the visitor's ID and types the number into the system. Then the system checks if the person is already in the database.

lines.speaker: Client
lines.line: And what happens if the person is not in the database?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: In that case, the guard creates a new record. After that, the system prints a badge with a QR code, and finally the visitor can enter.

lines.speaker: Client
lines.line: Why did you use a QR code instead of a normal card?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: Because QR codes are cheap and fast. Moreover, the guard can read them with a phone, so we don't need a special card reader.

lines.speaker: Client
lines.line: Sounds good. Are there any disadvantages?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: Yes, one. If there is no internet, the system cannot check the database. However, we save the data locally and sync it later, so nothing is lost.

lines.speaker: Client
lines.line: And what about equipment that visitors bring, such as laptops?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: We register it in a similar way. The guard takes a photo and writes down the serial number. As a result, we can check the item when the person leaves.

lines.speaker: Client
lines.line: Perfect. Thank you for the explanation.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: You're welcome. Also, I can send you a short manual with these steps if you want.
